commits.body:
Inbox rows carried very little information for their height. Measured on an

commits.body:
`StructuredResponseCardPolicy.evaluate` gained a required `deliveryPending`
parameter in 3d944f5, but three call sites in
StructuredResponseCardPolicyTests were not updated, so the whole AutoHubTests
target failed to compile with "missing argument for parameter

commits.headline: fix(heartbeat): guard the beat treatment math against non-finite input
commits.body:
HasTrustworthySignal, ComputeIsDistant, and ComputeShockwavePhase now
follow TrialGPhysicsMath's float.IsFinite convention: a non-finite
pulseAmplitude reads as no signal, a non-finite distanceMeters holds
the previous distance state, and a non-finite secondsSinceBeat reads
as an expired ring. Also widens PulseAmplitude_ScalesEveryWeightLinearly
to assert Ember and Shockwave scale with gain, not just Size.

commits.headline: feat(heartbeat): decide the beat treatment from player state
docs(heartbeat): cover the summon flash below the device rung
commits.body:
TriggerSummonFlash had no test outside the headset, so the half of the summon
that happens on the black hole was proven only by looking at it. Adds a PlayMode
test that trips the flash, asserts it reaches an unrouted renderer, and asserts
it decays back down.

commits.headline: docs(heartbeat): plan the heartbeat visual channels
commits.body:
Ten tasks, TDD order, from the pure treatment math through the shader
channels, the property-block writer, the dev-gated UDP tuning rig on 9011,
the HUD tuning page and the summon-arrival cue.

is judged: shaders can only be evaluated on the headset, and rebuilding to

commits.headline: docs(heartbeat): design the visual channels the beat can speak through
commits.body:
The heartbeat drives one channel today — uniform scale on a child
transform — so the lub-dub in ComputePulseEnvelope never reaches the
user. This spec gives the beat more channels, selects between them by
player state, adds a summon cue at the hands, and wires the lensing
distortion for the first time.

commits.body: Addresses two Codex P1 findings from PR #1048 review:

commits.headline: fix(policy): close review regressions
fix(policy): scope action-gate regressions
fix(policy): harden escalation and action gates
test(trial-g): pin that the recall indicator can actually draw
commits.body:
The recall's only feedback is the lasso's rope, borrowed. Both of its
preconditions fail silently: a null line array or an unresolved target
collider skips the draw and returns, so the hole would still fly back
with nothing to show the gesture had fired. Neither is visible from the
summon's own logic, and the existing composition test stopped at "the
three components resolved" — which a silently inert indicator passes.

commits.headline: feat(trial-g): zip the summon back on an eased sub-second curve
commits.body:
The recall drove through the lasso's Selected path, which is deliberately
gentle — 0.55 m/s, eased in over 0.3 s — because it is a manipulation. A
room crossing at that speed took about five seconds, which is why the
timeout was six. A recall is a restart, not a manipulation, so it gets its
own drive: a fixed 0.6 s flight regardless of distance, so the gesture
reads the same whether the hole is across the room or just out of reach.

commits.headline: fix(voice): surface aborted turns in web clients
fix(voice): exclude fast-ack from smoke turn-completion predicate
commits.body:
VOICE_FAST_ACK_ENABLE defaults to true, so the server emits a filler
transcript:done ("On it...", role assistant) the instant it accepts a turn.
The harness predicate only checked role === 'assistant', so it resolved on the
ack and sent the next turn while hybridProcessing was still true.

commits.headline: fix(voice): deliver partial text on transcript:aborted, not transcript:done
commits.body:
Codex P1 (1/2): the error path was terminating the stream with
`transcript:done`, the successful-completion contract. Clients treat that
as success — the web handler clears the streaming flag and POSTs the text
to the conversation store — so a truncated turn was persisted and
redisplayed as a finished reply.

commits.headline: fix(voice): drop audio for client-local-STT sessions instead of recovering
commits.body:
Making the localSTT skip real means `_vad === null` is a local-STT session's
permanent designed state, which parks it inside handleClientAudio's
`!session._vad` recovery branch for the life of the connection. That branch is
self-clearing (`recoveryInProgress` resets in a `.finally()`) and the skip
resolves in well under the 20ms frame interval, so every frame started a fresh
recovery cycle: measured 25 frames -> 25 session:recovered, 25 openai:connected,
25 "Auto-triggering" log lines. Only the

commits.headline: fix(voice): stop SIGKILLing audiotoolbox players on barge-in
commits.body:
Barge-in teardown SIGKILLed the ffmpeg audiotoolbox player whenever it
did not exit within a 1500ms grace budget. A SIGKILLed ffmpeg never runs
its cleanup, so its CoreAudio HAL client is stranded inside coreaudiod.

commits.headline: fix(claude): trim a pause_turn tail stripped of every tool block
commits.body:
Codex P1 on #1046: the Pass-3 trim only fired when the caller's history
ended on a user turn, so an assistant-final history that lost its
server-tool blocks to reconciliation survived as text/thinking only — a
bare prefill, which the API rejects with "This model does not support
assistant message prefill." That traded one 400 for another.

commits.headline: fix(voice): skip server VAD/STT init for local-STT clients
commits.body:
`initializeVoiceProvider` was called un-awaited from the connection handler,
and its skip guard read `session.metadata.client.localSTT` — which only
arrives later via `client:context`. The guard was therefore always false on
the real connection path, so every iOS session built a Silero VAD it never
fed.

commits.headline: fix(trial-g): resolve the summon targets from the composed descendant
commits.body:
The recall shipped inert. TrialGSummonController looked for the physics
controller on the spawned instance itself and the lasso controller in its
parents, but the black hole is composed three levels deep: the spawner
instantiates the interactable root, BlackHoleInteractionFactory adds the
grabbable and Rigidbody to that root, and BlackHoleVisualComposer then
instantiates the trial visual — which carries both controllers — under the
root's VisualAnchor. Every reference resolved null, so Update()

commits.headline: fix(claude): prune dangling tool_search references before the API call
commits.body:
Tool round 2+ died cross-surface (chat x6, Slack x1, voice x1 over five
days) with:

commits.headline: fix(voice): report failed hybrid turns on the Socket.IO wire
commits.body:
A voice turn that threw mid-stream was indistinguishable from a successful
one on the wire. `transcript:done` was only emitted on the success path and
guarded by `if (fullResponse)`, the catch emitted nothing, and
`agent:thinking { state: 'end' }` fires from `finally` either way. The client
was left holding an unterminated stream with no way to detect, retry, or
surface the failure — the only record was `logs/dev-all.log`.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): bind the prod code-object exemption, gate fund transfers, widen the anaphor
commits.body:
Codex round 15. All three findings are in code round 14 added, and all three
are fail-opens.

commits.headline: feat(trial-g): summon the black hole back with a two-handed pinch
commits.body:
Distance grab already works, but it is a ray: a hole behind you cannot be
acquired at all, so the one mechanic that could recover it is exactly the
one that cannot reach it. Pinching both hands now recalls the hole to the
same reachable head-relative pose the spawner and the out-of-bounds
recovery already use, from anywhere, with no aiming.

fix(autojack): close six more judge-gate fail-opens found by Codex
commits.body:
Round-14 review surfaced six enumerations that were incomplete on a
fail-open gate. Every edit moves in the fail-closed direction — a new

commits.headline: fix(autojack): scope the SHA exemption to one field
commits.body:
routingText() folds question, options, context and the task fields into
one '\n'-joined string, and the commit-context guards on the secrets rule
used [\s\S]* — so commit vocabulary in ANY folded field freed a
credential sitting in the question. A task title reading "Rebase onto
origin/main" was enough to auto-answer "Should I use token <40-hex>?".

commits.headline: fix(autojack): close three round-10 fail-opens in the human-risk gate
commits.body:
Each fix moves the gate in the fail-CLOSED direction rather than adding
another phrasing to an allowlist:

commits.headline: fix(voice): keep questions built from the assistant's own words
commits.body:
normalizeEchoComparableText() strips punctuation, so "Sounds good?" and
"Sounds good" reach every echo check byte-identical and no threshold can
separate them. Read the question mark off the raw transcript and gate above
all four branches -- exact-equality swallowed the bare question just as
readily as the filler branch swallowed "Uh, sounds good?".

commits.headline: fix(live,watch): serialize task merges and make the watch relay ordered
commits.body:
Four Codex P1 findings on aa3931e, all ordering/duplication hazards in paths
this PR already touches.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): invert the deploy gate from a verb allowlist to a denylist
commits.body:
The `<verb> the deploy` cue list was an enumerated allowlist sitting on a
fail-open gate, and it leaked three rounds running — 5 verbs, then 9, then
15 — because each round extended the list instead of changing its polarity.
At 15 verbs "kick off the deploy" and "go ahead with the deploy" still
reached the judge unattended. English has unboundedly many ways to say "do
it" and a small closed set of ways to say "about it", so the list is now a
denylist of prepositions and connectives: any other wo

commits.headline: fix(voice): gate short-reply echo suppression on filler, not coverage
commits.body:
The coverage ratio added for the noisy-echo case could not distinguish STT
filler from a real answer: "uh sounds good" (0.79), "yeah sounds good" (0.69)
and "no thank you" (0.75) all cleared 0.6, so genuine replies that merely
opened with the words the assistant had just spoken were discarded as echoes —
the same turn loss this PR exists to fix, in a narrower form.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): close clear Codex P1 gaps without reversing gate policy
commits.body:
Round 9 on #1040. Broaden vague-approval prefixes; exclude 40-char SHAs
from opaque credentials; page passive bought/purchased and skip attributive
purchase/buying nouns; scope privacy to prompt text; page reset --hard when
a clause break follows; allow production database/schema objects unless an
adapter/helper suffix marks a refactor.

commits.headline: fix(voice): suppress noisy echoes of short assistant replies
commits.body:
The reverse-containment check required the assistant's reply to be at
least 12 characters, and the run-coverage check below it requires a
20-character shared run. A short reply echoed back with STT noise on the
front cleared neither: "Sounds good" (11 chars) coming back as "Uh,
sounds good" failed exact equality, skipped the containment branch on
length, and produced an 11-char run under the 20-char floor. The echo
read as a genuine turn and the agent could answer its own voice.

commits.headline: fix(heart-rate): require evidence, not just state, to hold the rig
commits.body:
A Polar H10 lying unworn on a desk is paired, connected, subscribed --
and Streaming, because the BLE source sets that state the moment it
subscribes rather than when a beat arrives. CanTakeRigFrom gated on
state alone, so a dry strap locked the LAN bridge out permanently.
That is exactly the hardware-free test loop the bridge exists to
provide, defeated by a sensor nobody was wearing.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): resolve six Codex P1 tradeoffs in the human-risk gate
commits.body:
Round 8 on #1040. Vague approvals under risky task titles still page;
reset --hard "for recovery" no longer borrows the doc carve-out; rerun/
retry/restart the deploy pages; UUID+ordinary key stays free; buy idioms
and order-by sorting stay free; production-data binds verb to object in
ask text so context constraints cannot false-page local work.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): close five more Codex P1 fail-opens on the risk gate
commits.body:
Round 7 on #1040. Allow currency/amount before buy/purchase objects; match
reset ... --hard with intervening flags/refs; page all-numeric opaque
tokens next to credential vocabulary; expand deploy execution cues to
approve/proceed/launch; and treat production data/dataset as record nouns.

commits.headline: fix(whatsapp): exercise real adapter gating in Tier-2 smoke
commits.body:
The webhook smoke stubbed getAdapter to always return processed, so
regressions in WhatsAppAdapter.detectMention / isReplyToBot would stay
green. Use a SmokeWhatsAppAdapter that runs real parse + second-stage
gating and only stubs Claude/outbound I/O.

commits.headline: fix(voice): queue VAD reset behind tail; retry Chatterbox model load
commits.body:
Keep Silero reset/endSegment serialized with in-flight ONNX work by
enqueueing reset after the existing packet tail instead of replacing it.
Treat Chatterbox model_loaded:false as retryable during startup polling.

commits.headline: fix(agents): route task control from managed sites
fix(autojack): close seven Codex P1 fail-opens on the human-risk gate
commits.body:
Round 6 on #1040. Tighten the reset --hard doc carve-out so an unrelated
Document verb cannot exempt a later wipe; let buy/purchase take ordinary
nouns while scoping that rule (and sync/rename production-data) to
question/options/context so task titles cannot fold in; drop the mandatory
digit on opaque credential literals; page run/do/start the deploy; cover
synchronize/synchronise; and gate SSN/PHI privacy vocabulary.

commits.headline: fix(push): send the gateway credential to protected registry routes
commits.body:
899e853 put `requireAuth` in front of `POST /v1/device-tokens` and the new
`POST /v1/activity-tokens`. The gateway checks those against
PUSH_GATEWAY_API_KEY, but the app only ever sent the hub `apiKey` and no
gateway credential existed anywhere in Settings or UserDefaults. A gateway
deployed with its own secret therefore answered 401 to both device and Live
Activity registration, silently dropping push delivery.

commits.headline: test(slack): pin cleanMessage bot ID without env coupling
commits.body:
Local/dev checkouts resolve workspace bot identity (or an unresolved
placeholder) instead of SLACK_BOT_USER_ID, so the alias-normalization
assertion was environment-dependent.

commits.headline: fix(voice): serialize Silero VAD control ops with packet queue
commits.body:
Queue endSegment/reset behind the audio FIFO and invalidate pending
packets on reset so commit/clear cannot race queued ONNX processing.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): grow the black hole as the heart rate slows, and wire the LAN bridge
commits.body:
Slower heart, bigger black hole — the mapping the throb was built to carry.
As the smoothed rate falls from 90 to 55 bpm the Trial G art root grows
smoothly to 1.6x, easing on a 7-second half-life so it reads as breathing
rather than as twitching on ordinary respiratory variation. It multiplies
with the beat envelope, so a slow heart is a large black hole that is still
visibly beating. Neither multiplier touches the black hole's diameter, which
also sizes the SphereCollider used to grab it.

commits.headline: fix(voice): address Codex P1s on echo suppression
commits.body:
- Re-arm auto-sleep after suppressing an echo. speech-start and speech-stop
  both cancelScheduledSleep(), so the suppression branch was the only terminal
  path in processFinalTranscript leaving no timer armed — mic stayed hot
  indefinitely. The prior comment's premise was wrong: scheduleSleep() is the
  ordinary 45s idle timer, not forceSleep().

commits.headline: fix(slack): keep bot-ID detection working when the base class passes a message
commits.body:
PlatformAdapter.handleIncomingMessage now forwards the normalized message in
the positional slot SlackAdapter.detectMention treats as an explicit bot-ID
override, so its regex was built from "[object Object]" and aliased mention
tokens like <@U09CWNC42KE|auto_jack> stopped matching. Only a string is
treated as an override now.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): gate the passive voice, and stop doc wording from exempting execution
commits.body:
Codex round 5 on #1040. Four of the five findings are the same shape: a
rule enumerated the ACTIVE voice and English asked in the passive.

commits.headline: test(api): exercise the successful iOS task-response route
commits.body:
The route test only covered schema rejection, so the iOS routing
regression it was meant to guard could have returned unnoticed. Drive a
valid iOS response through the real router, bridge, and Prisma store on
a pushed throwaway schema, and assert the waiting task reaches the queue
resume instead of the bridge's interaction_request_not_found.

commits.headline: fix(sync): prune task cache to empty only on authoritative total==0
commits.body:
An empty `/v1/tasks` response could reconcile the local Task cache to empty
and wipe it. A degraded hub returning `200 {"tasks": []}` while its task
store is unavailable decodes to an authoritative-looking empty array, so
pruning on it caused the exact data loss this branch guards against.

commits.headline: fix(sync): reapply lifecycle/attention on stale task payloads
commits.body:
899e853 dropped the `applyLifecycleAndAttention` call from `mergeTask`'s
stale-payload branch (the early return taken when the remote `updatedAt` is
not newer than the local one). That branch is exactly how a terminal status
arriving on an older-stamped payload clears a stranded `needs_input`
attention, so tasks could stay parked in "needs you" forever after they
finished.

commits.headline: fix(api): forward terminal SSE sweeps to status-filtered clients
commits.body:
The reaper flips a task to interrupted/cancelled before emitting
task_stale/task_expired, so gating those events on the status filter
dropped the exact transition a status-filtered client needs to clear its
card. Match terminal sweeps on identity/platform only.

commits.headline: fix(voice): gate Chatterbox health on model_loaded; restore split-dropped config
commits.body: Address Codex P1 findings on #1032:

commits.headline: fix(whatsapp): fail closed when legacy reply identities are absent
commits.body:
An older bridge that omits both quotedIsFromMe and quotedSender left the
legacy fallback comparing two empty normalizations, so any quoted message
with an AutoJack-looking prefix counted as a verified bot reply. Require
both identities to be known before trusting that fallback.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): close two fail-open gate holes; bind prod scope to its noun
commits.body:
Codex round 4 on #1040. Two of the four findings were fail-open — the
direction this PR exists to close — and both came from the same mistake:
gating on an ALLOWLIST of phrasings, where anything unlisted escapes.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): bind buy/order/reset --hard to an object or an intent
commits.body:
Codex round 3 on #1040 filed four P1s, all the same false-positive shape as
round 2: a bare word folded in from a task title and paged every question
asked under that task. Three were introduced by this PR and are fixed here;
each was reproduced against merged main first to confirm it was a regression
and not the standing behaviour.

commits.headline: docs(verification): record dev Slack smoke
fix(agents): harden Cloudflare operator boundaries
feat(heart-rate): scan for an unpaired strap, and scope the docs to evidence
commits.body:
Until now the BLE bridge could only reach a strap this headset had already
bonded with, which made the transport useless on anyone else's device. It now
walks the bonded devices first (last-known-good address first, so the common
case stays fast) and falls back to an active BLE scan when none of them
exposes 0x180D. The scan is rate-guarded, runs in a 10 s window, and accepts a
device either on a 0x180D service-UUID advertisement or, as a second chance, on
a name that looks like a strap -- some

commits.headline: fix(autojack): scope the new gate rules to their target (Codex round 2)
commits.body:
Four P1 findings on the first cut of #1036, all the same defect in two
directions: a rule keyed off words appearing ANYWHERE in the text that
routingText() folds together, rather than off the thing being acted on.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): close 13 verified fail-open holes in the judge's human-risk gate
commits.body:
classifyQuestionRoute() auto-answers unless a denylist regex matches, so every
phrasing the list misses becomes an autonomous action by an already-authorized
worker — there is no second gate downstream. With JUDGE_MODE=live and
JUDGE_PROMOTE_ALL=true (the active local config), 15 of 17 Codex-named probes
reached the judge on merged main.

commits.headline: fix(voice): name the source of a bad smoke scenario and refresh the env sample
commits.body:
Codex P1: .env.example documented VOICE_CONVERSATION_SMOKE_SCENARIO=basic, a
value that was never a real scenario, so anyone who copied it would now hit
the fail-closed guard on every run. Replace the stale sample with the valid
names plus a migration note, and name the offending source in the error so an
operator who never typed --scenario knows it came from .env or their shell.

commits.headline: fix(voice): fail closed on an unknown conversation-smoke scenario name
commits.body:
An explicitly requested scenario that is not a builtin used to fall back to
the 4-turn default suite and could report pass, so the harness read as "the
scenario I asked for passed" when a different scenario ran. Distinguish an
explicit request from the implicit default and throw on an unknown explicit
name, listing the valid scenarios. Scenario files still win over an inherited
stale scenario name so voice-eval runs are unaffected.

chore: restore split leftovers on main

Bring back the parked mcp-tools registry refresh, college-bros agent

commits.headline: fix(agents): enforce escalation completion limits
docs(heart-rate): scope BLE status claims to the evidence that backs them
commits.body:
The permission-dialog row said verified on the strength of a focused
GrantPermissionsActivity, which does not identify which permission it
belongs to. Closed by elimination instead: every other runtime permission
reads granted=true after the reinstall and only the two Bluetooth ones read
false, so no other permission is left for that dialog to be. The reasoning
is now in the row rather than the conclusion alone.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): direct BLE bridge, permission wait, and provenance HUD
commits.body:
Lands the Java half of the direct-BLE transport, fixes a race that would have
made the first launch after install fail every time, and adds an in-headset
readout that says where the heartbeat came from.

Skip writes after client close, and resolve ledger/queue tasks before

Switch offline defaults to dana_escalating / Fred Rezone, add Parakeet

commits.headline: fix(whatsapp): native mentions and quotedIsFromMe reply gating
commits.body:
Use bridge-provided quotedIsFromMe and mentionedJIDs so group replies and
@mentions activate reliably without relying on owner-number heuristics alone.

commits.headline: fix(live): reopen attention when task re-enters needs-input
commits.body:
When a task_changed (or legacy agent_task) event moves a task back into a
needsInput-normalized status after a prior prompt was resolved, the merge
handlers only updated task.status and left the stale attentionResolvedAt set.
Task.requiresUserAttention rejects any task with a non-nil resolved marker, so
the re-opened prompt never resurfaced. Mirror the mergeTaskStatusUpdate path:
on a needsInput transition, reset attentionResolvedAt and establish the
fallback attentionType. Applies the same fix

commits.headline: fix(autojack): gate judge promotion on the active model's own rows
commits.body:
Codex P1: `promote` was computed from the whole calibration window, so a
window spanning the Opus->Sonnet flip could put the new judge live on a
record it never earned. 19 correct Opus rows plus 1 incorrect Sonnet row
reads as 95% over 20 samples and promotes Sonnet on an 0/1 record of its
own. `mixedModel` was only informational, and no operator is in the
JudgePromotionController.refresh() -> getMode() -> auto-answer path, so an
operator-visible warning could not guard it.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): close gate holes from narrowing + fix replay dedup
commits.body:
Codex P1s on the narrowed HUMAN_RISK_PATTERNS. Narrowing the gate to stop
paging on routine dev vocabulary also opened three holes that are not policy
changes — each one is a documented Red-tier invariant (AGENTS.md) and is on the
judge profile's own escalate list ("money movement, secret exposure, destroying
data, or contacting real third parties"). #1028 also force-promotes to live
auto-answering, so these are reachable without Jack, not theoretical.

commits.body:

commits.headline: test(voice): guard sleep-timer invariant the echo suppressor relies on
commits.body:
The assistant-echo suppression path no longer calls scheduleSleep() when it
discards a transcript — doing so ended the session outright whenever the
classification was wrong. That is only safe because the sleep timer armed when
the assistant finished speaking survives interrupt() and still fires.

commits.headline: fix(runtime): resolve Codex P2 findings on task/watch paths
commits.body:
- removeTasks: decode TaskLifecycleEventPayload with the flexible
  hub-date strategy (matching mergeSnapshot/mergeSingleTask/

- push-gateway: gitignore the runtime-written activity-tokens.json
  (APNs Live Activity tokens), mirroring device-tokens.json.
- watch sendTextToPhone: on a transport error, hand the prompt to
  transferUserInfo (OS-durable, FIFO) instead of only persistin

commits.headline: test(voice): use mic-proven phrases in echo_vocabulary_reuse

builtin scenarios already use because they survive the mic path intact.

commits.headline: feat(autojack): flip the judge from Opus to Sonnet 5
commits.body:
Sonnet 5 is near-Opus on this kind of bounded, evidence-bound call at ~1/1.7
the cost, and the judge runs on every routed question. This changes judge
quality characteristics -- that is the point, and it is now measurable rather
than assumed.

commits.headline: feat(autojack): record the concrete judge model on every calibration row
commits.body:
Agreement rate is a property of the judge, not just the decision class.
calibration.js buckets on decisionClass alone, so a window spanning a model
change averages two different judges into one number -- and judge-promotion.js
could promote a class to live on that mixed sample. This adds the column that
makes a pre/post comparison possible at all, and must land before the judge's
model changes.

commits.headline: test(voice): add echo_vocabulary_reuse Tier-2 regression scenario
commits.body:
Probes the 2026-07-25 vanishing-transcript failure: a real user turn that
reuses the assistant's own vocabulary must survive the echo suppressor and
get a reply.

commits.headline: fix(voice): stop echo suppressor from deleting real user turns
commits.body:
The realtime CLI was discarding complete, quality-gated final transcripts
as "assistant echo," which dropped the turn AND put the session to sleep —
the user saw their transcript vanish mid-conversation and the agent go
silent. data/voice-transcript.log has 58 of these; replaying the last 12
against their real assistant pairs shows all 12 came through the token
path, none through substring containment.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): keep synthetic traffic out of the replay denominator
commits.body:
The Tier-2 smoke deliberately leaves its telemetry row in `events` — that
row IS the evidence. But judge-routing-replay.mjs reads the same table, so
the synthetic refund question was being counted as real recorded traffic,
landing in both the BEFORE-pages numerator and the denominators of the
harness this branch just made honest about its coverage.

commits.headline: test(autojack): Tier-2 smoke proving human-risk pages are auditable
commits.body:
The unit test for the basePayload fix asserts on an injected telemetryBus, so
it cannot prove what actually lands in the events table — the entire point of
the change. This drives the real router with a real telemetry sink against the
real DB and reads the row back.

commits.body:
Wires the heart-rate SDK into Trial G so pressing Play produces a visible
pulse with no sensor, no bridge and no fixture.

commits.headline: fix(heart-rate): record verbatim wire frames instead of re-encoded measurements
commits.body:
Integrating the two transports surfaced a real flaw in the SDK seam. The capture
recorder could only observe MeasurementReceived, which is already decoded, so a
"recorded" fixture actually held OUR canonical re-encoding of the strap's data
rather than the strap's own bytes.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): UDP bridge transport and host-side replay tool
commits.body:
Adds the companion-device path: a UDP listener whose datagram payload is a raw
0x2A37 frame. Deliberately dumb and transport-only, so one socket serves the
simulator, a Mac bridge, Home Assistant, or a Pulsoid relay without any further
Unity code.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): direct on-device BLE transport behind a testable seam
commits.body:
Adds the standalone-on-Quest path: the headset connects straight to a BLE Heart
Rate Profile strap over its own Bluetooth radio, no companion phone or PC.

commits.headline: feat(heart-rate): shared BLE heart-rate SDK with hardware-free simulation
commits.body:
Foundation for driving the black hole pulse from the wearer's real heartbeat.
Verified research established there is no first-party Meta/OpenXR heart-rate or
PPG API on any Quest, and that pupillometry (Quest 3 has no eye tracking; Quest
Pro exposes gaze pose only) and on-headset camera rPPG (passthrough cameras face
outward, away from the wearer) are dead ends. The only real signal is an external
BLE Heart Rate Profile sensor, service 0x180D / characteristic 0x2A37.

commits.body:
com.unity.xr.management@4.4.0 declares a dependency on com.unity.modules.vr,
which does not exist in Unity 6 — blocking package resolution even after the
direct vr entry was removed. Both XR pins are 2022.3-era and unneeded at compile
time; OpenXR is re-added at the correct version when the provider is enabled in
XR Plug-in Management.

commits.headline: Fix Unity 6 package resolve: meta.xr.sdk.core@203 + drop dead vr module
commits.body:
The all-in-one meta-package com.meta.xr.sdk.all was retired from Meta's npm
registry ('no such package available'); depend on com.meta.xr.sdk.core@203.0.0
(min Unity 6000.0.66f2, pulls com.unity.xr.hands) which provides the OVR* types.
com.unity.modules.vr does not exist in Unity 6 (XR moved to packages) — removed.
Fixes 'Project has invalid dependencies' on open.
